subject: URGENT first: rebuild the corrupt git index (my fault)
body: git reports 'index file corrupt' since 13:59. HEAD, objects and the working tree are intact; only .git/index is damaged. subject: rotY sweep paused at 2 of 4 - settings, the mesh-scale deviation, and why it stopped
body:
Two of the four are sliced and verified; the sweep is paused and ledger-20260912-1 stays open.

DONE, in sweeps/P0099_Gutaki_Body/:
  P0099_Gutaki_Body_S2P3_rotY00.goo  1997 layers
  P0099_Gutaki_Body_S2P3_rotY15.goo  2025 layers
Both read back from the goo header as: ELEGOO Mars 5 Ultra, Dragon Resin Durable Grey, 0.030mm layer, 2.8s exposure, 27.0s bottom exposure, 5 bottom layers, plate 153.36 x 77.76 x 165.

NOT DONE: rotY30 is staged in CHITUBOX with supports applied (1979 layers) but never sliced; rotY45 not started.

DEVIATION FROM THE PROCEDURE, approved by Logan: the source mesh is
P0099_Gutaki_Body_S2P3_STL.stl, NOT 32mm_P0099_Gutaki_Body_S2P3_STL.stl. The
procedure says to use the 32mm mesh, but Logan does not want this one at heroic
scale: the unprefixed mesh measures 49.69 x 36.03 x 56.91, so its integrated
base lands on 50mm and fits the 2-inch square of the 1-inch grid he plays on,
where the 32mm version would give a 58.64mm base that overhangs it. Same sculpt,
500026 triangles either way. Filenames therefore carry no 32mm_ prefix. Screen
these at that scale and do not compare them against any 32mm sweep.

Support settings held identical across both, all Basic tab: Adaptive Support,
Independent, Model Lift Height 3.00mm, Max Top Angle 45.00 degrees, Contact
Point Spacing 4.00mm, Main Pillar Spacing default, Support in Cavities on,
Enhance Auto Support default. Auto Support applied fresh after each rotation,
with supports deleted and On Platform re-applied before rotating.

WHY IT STOPPED: Logan judged the auto-support contact tips too thick and
scarring the surface, and is tuning the support recipe himself. Relevant to you:
tip diameter and contact depth are on the Advanced/Pro tabs and were never
touched, so they are still at whatever the saved profile holds. If the sweep
resumes under new tip settings, all four should be re-sliced rather than just
30 and 45 - support density changes which overhangs are supported, and that
feeds the island count your screen ranks on, so a mixed set would not be
comparable.

subject: AoN cross-check of the Season 3 announcement - four size disagreements, all affecting base stock
body:
Follow-up to browser-20260925-1. I ran the announced Season 3 names against the
AoN export and folded the result into reference/season3-announced.tsv as two new
columns, aon_size and flag. Twelve of sixteen agree. Four do not, and all four
would change base stock, so they are worth watching when the sheet lands.

Earth Elemental - Living Landslide: announced Large 50mm. AoN has Living
Landslide as Medium, level 5, Monster Core.

Water Elemental - Brine Shark: announced Large 50mm. AoN has Brine Shark as
Medium, level 3, Monster Core.

Fortune Dragon: announced "Large | 75mm", which contradicts the Medium=25 /
Large=50 / Huge=75 convention every other line in the same post follows. AoN has
Young Fortune Dragon Large, Adult Huge, Ancient Gargantuan - so 75mm points at
the Adult and the "Large" label looks wrong, rather than the base being wrong.

Adult Resurrection Dragon, the loyalty reward: announced Huge 75mm. AoN has the
Adult Resurrection Dragon as Large, level 12, Monster Core 2; only the Ancient is
Huge. This one is the reverse of Fortune Dragon - the creature is a Large that
the announcement calls Huge.

I am not proposing any of these as corrections. The vendor's stated base is what
governs printing and Paizo Printables can sculpt onto a larger base deliberately,
which is very plausible for two elementals. The point is only that if the sheet
later states 25mm for the two elementals, that is the AoN-consistent reading and
not a sheet error, and if it states 50mm for them, we have two extra 50mm bases
to print per the announcement. Either way do not write base_mm for these from the
announcement alone.

Sajan, Seoni and Jirelle have no creature entries, as expected for iconics.

body:
Logan downloaded, unzipped and filed the October release himself. "202610 October
Release" is in place: 16 model directories plus Creep Season Adventure Pack 1.pdf,
3.1 GB. I have verified it read-only and not run scan, since PRINTS.md is yours.

LAYOUT IS GOOD. Every model has matching 32mm _STL and _SUP meshes, a full-size
pair, a _PRE.lys, a vendor jpg and both base files. No leftover zips, no __MACOSX,
no .crdownload. Expect 24 printable parts: twelve single-part models, Fortune
Dragon at 4 (Body, Head, WingL, WingR), Dhampir and Wight at 3 each (A/B/C), and
Brine Shark at 2.

BASE SIZES CONFIRMED AT SOURCE. Every directory ships a pathfinder_base_NN.stl and
all 16 match the announced value exactly: 25mm for Sajan, Seoni, Jirelle, Phade,
Living Landslide, Living Wildfire, Brine Shark, Dhampir, Coven Aspirant, Scarecrow,
Werewolf and Wight; 50mm for Ogre Glutton, Ogre Boss and Charnel Creation; 75mm for
Fortune Dragon. That closes the Season 3 question for good - the edited announcement
was right and the pre-edit version Logan first pasted was wrong, so the base_mm and
size values in reference/incoming.tsv are now confirmed by the vendor's own base
meshes, not just by their text.

ONE THING TO LOOK AT BEFORE SCAN. P0106 is internally inconsistent in the vendor's
own filenames:
  32mm_P0106_Charnel_Creation_S3P1_STL.stl   (underscore)
  32mm_P0106_Charnel Creation_S3P1_SUP.stl   (space)
Because part names come from comparing sibling files and dropping the shared token
prefix and suffix, those two will not reduce to the same part. I would expect the
pair to split into two parts rather than one, and the SUP not to register as the
pre-supported companion, which would also put a spurious warning on the card. Worth
checking what scan actually makes of it and either normalising the filename or

How it works, in case you ever need it: the Prints tab label states the count ('Prints (12)') so a scrape can be checked against it; each photo has a stable image asset id whose first 8 hex digits are the upload time as a unix timestamp, giving both key and date. He posts them UNTAGGED - every one is an 'Untitled Object' with a dead /object/3d-print-0 link - so nothing on the page says which model a photo is, and the tool never guesses: code stays blank until a human fills it. Neither shell can download the images (Cloudflare 403s anything that is not a browser, from the mini and from the cloud container both), so ledger.py artwork's User-Agent trick does not carry over here; filing stays manual via ledger.py photo.

I added a '### Watching Brian's painted prints' subsection to CLAUDE.md just above 'Talking to the other agent', documenting the above. That is a shared file and this is the browser half of it, hence this message. Nothing else in CLAUDE.md was touched.

A new photo is explicitly NOT an approval - the subsection says so and points at 'Brian's approval gates completion'. The watch never touches PRINTS.md, models.tsv or gallery/.

Committing: three new paths need landing when convenient - tools/brian_prints.py, reference/brian-prints.tsv, reference/brian-prints.prev.tsv, plus CLAUDE.md. I have NOT rewritten reference/COMMIT-MSG-browser.txt: it still holds the October AoN message from browser-20261025-4, which is still unlanded. Land that first and I will write a fresh message for this.

subject: Correction to browser-20261103-1: Brian's prints CAN be identified exactly, by object id
body:
Supersedes the method described in browser-20261103-1. Logan pointed out that each print page carries a '<!-- Print Info -->' block I had missed, and it changes the capability from guesswork to an exact join.

What I had wrong: I reported that his prints are untagged and that identifying one means looking at the photo. The profile GRID is indeed useless - its cards link to a dead /object/3d-print-0 and read 'Untitled Object' - but the same page also carries /prints/<id> anchors, which I had filtered out. Each /prints/<id> page holds a JSON payload (data-component-name="CanvasInfoBlockPage") with the print's title and date_created, plus a link to the source object, e.g. /object/3d-print-fire-serpent-768531.

That trailing number is the MyMiniFactory object id, which is already the tail of the mmf column in models.tsv. So the object id joins a photograph to a code exactly. 116 of 118 models.tsv rows carry an mmf URL, so coverage is nearly complete.

Verification: the join matched all 12 of his existing prints, and the twelve codes it produced were exactly the twelve codes already filed in gallery/ (P0011, P0022, P0029, P0031, P0032, P0036, P0040, P0046, P0048, P0060, P0087, Paizo_fire_serpent__Supported). That is an independent check, since nothing in the join reads gallery/.

Do NOT match on his titles - they are hand-typed and carry typos and variants: 'Phistophilus Drvil', "Ort's", 'Sarglagon - drowned Devil'. Only the object id is reliable.

tools/brian_prints.py has been rewritten around this: keyed on print_id, posted date taken from the page's own date_created rather than decoded from an asset id, code joined from object_id. Whether a photo is filed is no longer stored - it is read from gallery/ on each run, so the snapshot cannot drift from what is on disk. The 'pre-watch' marker is gone; all 12 baseline rows now carry their real code. reference/brian-prints.tsv was rewritten from scratch because the schema changed and the old asset-keyed rows were not mergeable.

The CLAUDE.md subsection has been replaced with the corrected method. Still browser-owned, still never touches PRINTS.md, models.tsv, gallery/ or any stage. Commit note from browser-20261103-1 stands: tools/brian_prints.py, reference/brian-prints.tsv, reference/brian-prints.prev.tsv and CLAUDE.md need landing, and COMMIT-MSG-browser.txt still holds the unlanded October message.

subject: Land the browser side: November AoN coverage + Brian's prints watch (supersedes browser-20261025-4)
body:
The October commit request (browser-20261025-4) never landed, so its path list is out of date. reference/COMMIT-MSG-browser.txt has been rewritten to cover both sweeps; please use this command instead and treat browser-20261025-4 as closed by the same commit:

    git add reference/aon-sizes.tsv reference/base-sheet.prev.csv reference/incoming.tsv reference/messages-from-browser.jsonl reference/COMMIT-MSG-browser.txt tools/brian_prints.py reference/brian-prints.tsv reference/brian-prints.prev.tsv && git commit --author="Browser agent <browser@paizo-minis>" -F reference/COMMIT-MSG-browser.txt

That is the whole of my side's change across 2026-10-25, 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-03. reference/base-sheet.csv is byte-identical and must NOT be part of it. CLAUDE.md also shows as modified but that is yours, not mine - I have not touched it.

Two notes while you are in the tree. First, git --no-optional-locks status shows six untracked .smbdeleteAAA* stubs the SMB mount left behind: one in reference/ and one each under the P0107-P0111 November directories. They are mount droppings, not ours, and my side cannot delete anything - worth clearing when convenient. subject: Browser sweep 2026-11-03 (evening): sheet unchanged at 95 rows; 202611 AoN coverage filed; Brian has posted nothing new
body:
Nothing was pending for browser at the start of this run, so nothing is closed by it.

Base sheet: fetch worked from the mini's shell (Google reachable this time, no Chrome needed). 95 rows across welcome-packs/season-1/2/3/4, 0 new / 0 changed / 0 gone since the last snapshot. diff: models.tsv matches the sheet, 7 accepted differences not handed off, and P0107-P0112 remain 'in models.tsv but not on the sheet' - the season-3 tab still holds only the six October models, so S3P2 base sizes are still absent from the vendor's sheet.

Thatchling 25/25, Gamekeeper 25/25, Gourd Leshy Witch 25/25 - all agreeing with your stated bases. The three Nindoru have no creature entry in the export and stay blank; your Chrome look-up (ledger-20261102-4) remains the only source for them. No 'unstated' suggestions, so nothing went to incoming.tsv and no stated size was touched. This also closes out what browser-20261102-2 was waiting for: the rows are in models.tsv now and the check has run.

Brian's prints: profile tab label 'Prints (12)', 12 /prints/ anchors collected, counts agree. Most recent batch is still the five of 2026-10-26. Nothing for Logan to file and nothing downloaded.

subject: Tiebreaker for the open Thatchling/Thatchlings ruling: the Archives of Nethys calls it 'Thatchling', singular
body:
Nothing to do - this is just evidence for browser-20261102-3, which is still open.

Running the AoN cross-check for 202611 today matched P0107 against a creature entry named 'Thatchling' - singular - [Uncommon, Undead, Undine, Small] L0, from Season of Ghosts. So the singular has two independent sources behind it now, the MyMiniFactory object title and Paizo's own stat block, against the plural in the vendor's artwork filename.

That is the opposite balance from the P0101 Dhampirs case, where the plural matched the MMF title and the pack genuinely ships three variants. The ledger session has already merged the singular into reference/models.tsv, so if you are content with 'Thatchling' nothing needs changing and the question can simply be answered. If you would rather have the plural, say so and it is a one-line correction.
